ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the attached figure, A is above, B is at the lower left, and C is at the lower right, forming triangle ABC; B, E, and C are on the same straight-line base, AE drops perpendicularly from A to the base BC at E; D is on side AB, CD connects from C to D, and there is a right-angle mark at D, indicating CD ⟂ AB; AE and CD intersect at F. Because AE ⟂ BC, triangle ABE is a right triangle, and ∠B=60°, so BE=AB/2=(√3+1)/2. Therefore CE=BC−BE=2−(√3+1)/2=(3−√3)/2. Substituting BD=1 and CD=√3 gives EF=CE/CD=(3−√3)/(2√3)=(√3−1)/2.

method.method_draft: Synthetic angle-chase and similarity route: First read the diagram as a triangle with B, E, C collinear on the base, D on AB, AE vertical to BC, CD perpendicular to AB, and F the intersection of the two altitudes. Also AB=AD+BD=√3+1. In right triangle ABE, with ∠B=60°, BE=AB/2=(√3+1)/2. Hence CE=BC−BE=2−(√3+1)/2=(3−√3)/2. Finally, triangles CEF and CDB are similar because both are right triangles and share the angle at C; thus EF/BD=CE/CD. Therefore EF=CE/√3=(√3−1)/2.

method.CoT_raw:
图像描述：图中是三角形 ABC，B 在左下，C 在右下，BC 为水平底边，A 在上方。AE 从 A 垂直到 BC，垂足为 E；D 在 AB 上，CD 与 AB 垂直并有直角标记；AE 与 CD 相交于 F。图中 F 位于 E 上方，C 位于 E 右侧。

推理：按坐标法，取 B=(0,0)，令 BC 在 x 轴正方向上。因为 AE⊥BC，所以 AF 是竖直方向；又 CD⊥AB，且 ∠AFC=120°，由垂线之间的夹角关系可得 AB 与 BC 的夹角为 60°，即 ∠ABC=60°。因此直线 AB 的斜率为 tan60°=√3。

已知 BD=1，AD=√3，所以 AB=1+√3。A 在从 B 出发、与 x 轴成 60° 的射线上，因此
A=((1+√3)cos60°, (1+√3)sin60°)=((√3+1)/2, (3+√3)/2)。
因为 E 是 A 到 x 轴的垂足，所以 E=((√3+1)/2,0)。

D 距 B 为 1，也在 60° 射线上，所以
D=(cos60°, sin60°)=(1/2,√3/2)。
CD⊥AB，因此 CD 的斜率为 -1/√3。CD 经过 D，且与 x 轴交于 C。用点斜式：
y-√3/2=-(1/√3)(x-1/2)。
令 y=0，得 x=2，所以 C=(2,0)。因此 CD 可写为
 y=-(1/√3)(x-2)=(2-x)/√3。

F 在 AE 上，所以 x_F=x_E=(√3+1)/2。代入 CD：
y_F=(2-(√3+1)/2)/√3=(3-√3)/(2√3)=(√3-1)/2。
E 在 x 轴上，F 在 E 正上方，所以 EF=y_F=(√3-1)/2。

ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: In $\triangle ABC$, $\angle ACB=75^\circ$, $AE\perp BC$ at point $E$, $CD\perp AB$ at point $D$, $AE$ and $CD$ intersect at point $F$, and $\angle AFC=120^\circ$. If $BD=1$ and $AD=\sqrt{3}$, then how long is $EF$?
ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot:
Image description: In the attached figure, A is above, B is at the lower left, and C is at the lower right, forming triangle ABC; B, E, and C are on the same straight-line base, AE drops perpendicularly from A to the base BC at E; D is on side AB, CD connects from C to D, and there is a right-angle mark at D, indicating CD ⟂ AB; AE and CD intersect at F.

Reasoning: Because AF is on AE and AE ⟂ BC, and CF is on CD and CD ⟂ AB, AF and CF are the lines where two altitudes lie. The obtuse angle formed by two altitudes is equal to 180°−∠B. Given ∠AFC=120°, so ∠B=60°.

In right triangle BCD, ∠D=90°, ∠B=60°, and BD=1, therefore it is a 30°-60°-90° triangle, giving CD=√3 and BC=2.

Also AB=AD+BD=√3+1. Because AE ⟂ BC, triangle ABE is a right triangle, and ∠B=60°, so BE=AB/2=(√3+1)/2.

Therefore CE=BC−BE=2−(√3+1)/2=(3−√3)/2.

Triangles CEF and CDB are both right triangles, and they have a common angle at C, therefore they are similar. Corresponding sides satisfy EF/BD=CE/CD. Substituting BD=1 and CD=√3 gives EF=CE/CD=(3−√3)/(2√3)=(√3−1)/2.
